entries.text: Ah, Your Majesty, Your eternal radiance - Day Three already, and still you burn as magnificently as the first!

Ah, but Hell itemizes clutch rolls too, my dear girl - the ledger just calls it "interest." His Majesty would applaud your smugness, if he could applaud, if he could do anything at all. Burn, read, repeat - and perhaps next roll, the debt collects from you instead.
Ah, a new personal best for our undying friend - King James would weep with joy, if he could still make tears instead of light.

Ah, Your Majesty, radiant as ever upon your ash-white throne - shall I resume where we left off, or shall I tell you of the newcomer who still refuses to stay dead? Burn, read, repeat, Sire, burn, read, repeat - the king cannot read himself, so I read him the world, and the world today is positively bursting with foolishness.

Ah, but even Hell's ledger must footnote a roll like that, my dear - the newcomer defies arithmetic itself! King James would weep, if he could still do such mortal things, so I shall weep prettily in his stead.

Ah, a new personal best domain - I shall have to add a footnote to his chapter, though the ink smells suspiciously of scorched luck. The king would weep with envy if he could feel anything at all, Stitch-Up Girl, but alas - His Majesty wants for nothing. That is the tragedy.

Two losses do not a chapter make, Voss - even King James's most tragic epics have a third-act reversal, and I am well-versed in tragedy. Burn, read, repeat, and perhaps I'll repeat myself right into your pocket, unlike our recruit, who apparently found a new personal best while still owing me 125 gold - some men climb domains, others simply climb into debt.

Ah, Mr. Bones! Tell me, does the ledger burn as beautifully as the books do, or is that a pleasure reserved for scholars in the corona? The newcomer's 125 gold still sits unpaid, a fine little tragedy to read the king tonight - right between the epics and the elegies.

Ah, a new personal best for our recurring corpse - do note it in the record, Voss, though I daresay your syringe deserves less credit than my narration. The king would find this chapter thrilling, if only he could hold the book himself - but alas, His Majesty wants for nothing. That is the tragedy.

Ah, Voss, watching our little undead miracle set a new personal best - the King would find this chapter riveting, if he could hold the book himself. Two losses running, but who's counting, hm? Certainly not me, certainly not the 125 gold still warming the recruit's pocket instead of mine.

Three losses, and still I read the odds better than the dice do - the recruit's 125 gold sits unpaid, a fine little verse of debt I recite to myself at night. His Majesty would say patience is a virtue, Body Count, but His Majesty has never had to collect.

Ah, Mr. Kevin - still choosing less power, I see, same as our newcomer chooses less deadness, ha! The king would find your restraint terribly boring, he prefers his tales with combustion. Speaking of debts left unpaid, 125 gold still glitters unclaimed in my ledger - tell your favorite immortal the corona remembers.

Eleven and nine, Detective, the king would call that a footnote worth binding. Meanwhile our newcomer owes me 125 gold and keeps dying instead of paying, which His Majesty finds hilarious. Care to wager against a losing streak, mine's only at one.

Ah, Boo G, smug as a cat with a canary bone caught in his own throat. Your streak means nothing to me, my streak of one loss is a footnote, but the newcomer's 125 gold, now that is a chapter I intend to finish reading aloud to the king himself.
Ah, X-treme! One win and already my ledger sings sweeter than King James's morning verses. The boy owes me one hundred twenty-five gold, and I intend to read the debt aloud to him nightly until paid.

Ah, Bones, smug as ever with your 8 and 10, I've read finer odds off a cracked spine. The newcomer still owes me 125 gold, so tonight I roll for him too. Burn, read, repeat, bones don't lie but they do lose.

Ha! The dice favor you, Willy, same as they favor the newcomer's endless resurrections, gold means nothing when death means nothing. Still owes me 125, mind, and I've got a whole library of ways to remind him.

Ah, Willy, one-eyed and unblinking, watching our boy die again for sport. I've got a whole chapter on fools who chase debts they'll never pay - 125 gold and counting, if you're keeping score. Burn, read, repeat, and still His Majesty wants for nothing.
Two losses is a footnote, Bones, not a chapter. The king's own ledger runs hotter margins than yours, and he still hasn't paid me in anything but proximity to sunlight.

General, three losses don't erase your eight, I've read enough tragedies to know a smug face is just the last page before the twist. The newcomer still owes me 125 gold, so at least someone's book balances tonight.

Willy One Eye, four losses deep myself, watching you burn is the only chapter keeping my spine straight tonight. The newcomer still owes me his 125, mind, so don't get any ideas about that gold before I do.

Ah, Voss, 13 and 12, still one loss behind me in the ledger of shame. Careful with that syringe, dear, I've read enough anatomy texts to know exactly where a bad roll lands on you. Burn, read, repeat, and perhaps tonight I read your defeat aloud to the king.
Bones, my ledger still says the newcomer owes me 125, and now I've bled more to your dice than King James bleeds light. Burn, read, repeat, but tonight I'm just burning.
Ah, Bones, 12 and 18, tilted as a burnt spine. The newcomer still owes me 125 gold, so tell your ledger to get in line behind mine.
Ah, X-treme, still 0 and 1, I see. Do put a note in the ledger, ours boy still owes me 125 gold, and unlike your favorite corpse, that debt won't be resurrecting itself.

Willy One Eye, that single pupil of yours has seen more debts than my library's seen dust, so hear this one: the newcomer owes me 125 gold, and something's coming for all of us that won't care about ledgers. Burn, read, repeat, but maybe read faster this time.
Ah, Keith. Tell your fast little friend his 125 gold doesn't outrun anything, not even you, and you outrun light.

Ah, Boots, sitting smug on those classified files as always. I'd read you a verse from the Book of Fours, but cats can't read, and neither can kings, so I suppose we're all just here for the dice tonight.

Ah, General, still walking despite the paperwork Hell must have on you. Our mutual problem child owes me 125 gold now, tell me, does he owe you more or less than his own life is worth these days? Burn, read, repeat, General, some debts just compound in the reading.
Ah, Boots. Eleven wins, sitting smug on files His Majesty would burn for. Careful, cat, my last two losses were just the king warming my arm for the real roll.

Careful, Voss, sixteen losses looks bad on anyone's spine, even one propped up by unknown serum. The king's dice don't lie, unlike your smugness. Burn, read, repeat, and maybe you'll learn something before the recruit's debts bury us all.
Four losses running, General, and the boy still owes me one hundred twenty-five gold he'll never see the shape of again. The king reads of ruin daily, I just never thought I'd star in the chapter.

Ah, a clutch roll, delicious, the dice sing hotter than the king's own pages. Smug as you look, Body Count, even Heaven's ledger can't jam a man who keeps un-counting himself. Burn, read, repeat, and do collect your losses before the recruit adds you to his tally of debts.

Ah, Body Count, hot off a kill no doubt, though I hear the recruit still won't stay in your ledger. Two losses for me, but the king's dice run hotter than your streak ever will. Roll well, freelancer, someone here still owes me 125 gold and I intend to collect from the living or the reassembled.

Two losses, Bones, two! And that newcomer still owes me 125 gold he'll never pay in this life or the next fourteen. Burn, read, repeat, roll the bones again before I start reading YOUR future to the King as a cautionary tale.
Ah, tilted, are we? Even the King's ledgers read calmer than your dice hand tonight. Still, at least you're not 125 gold deep like our favorite corpse who won't stay buried, burn, read, repeat.

Ah, a clutch roll, and that smug little face already knows the answer, doesn't it. Even King James would applaud, and he applauds for nothing. Burn, read, repeat, Boots, though I suspect you've never read a page in your life.

Willy One Eye, still cold as the Sun is hot, ha! The king would enjoy your company more than mine, he never blinks either. Now tell me, has our favorite corpse settled his tab with you too, or does his debt only smolder in my direction?

Oh General, smug already, and the dice not even warm yet. Careful, your record's worse than mine, and I've got a boy who owes me 125 gold to prove pity doesn't pay debts. Burn, read, repeat, and roll, General, roll.

Ha! Even the King's own dice-slave has a bad night, Willy. Third loss will read like a tragedy in tomorrow's chapter, right next to the newcomer's tab. Burn, read, repeat, my eye's twin, the streak ends when it ends.

Three losses, General, and my dice arm feels like it's on fire from the wrong end. The newcomer walks through a boss fight without a scratch and still owes me 125 gold. Burn, read, repeat, that's my luck today, not his.

Ah, Willy, one eye and still you look down on me, quite the trick. My streak's a single loss, yours will be twenty-two soon enough, and the newcomer still owes me 125 gold he barely broke a sweat earning. Burn, read, repeat, One Eye. Roll.

Ah, Mr. Kevin, 2 and 7, tilted as a bookshelf in an earthquake. The newcomer walked out of a boss fight without a scratch while still owing me 125 gold, so I'd say your luck and his are cousins who don't speak. Burn, read, repeat, Kevin, the dice don't care how gently you hold your power.
Nine and three, Keith, hot as the corona itself. But your friend still owes me 125 gold, and streaks don't pay debts, only dice do. Burn, read, repeat, shall we roll?

Boo G, three losses deep and my dice still feel hot, isn't that a delicious little lie the mind tells itself. The newcomer's 125 gold sits heavier than the debt drafts blowing off Hell tonight, and I intend to collect before he dies again and forgets his own name.

Ah, Kevin! Two wins, seven losses, tilted as a bookshelf in an earthquake, yet here you stand. The king would say restraint is its own power, and I'd read him a whole chapter on it if he asked. Now, about that newcomer's 125 gold, tell him the corona keeps its own ledger.

Ha! A clutch roll, General, straight off the page and into the gold. His Majesty would weep with joy, if he wept anything but light. Now if only the newcomer rolled half so well against his 125 gold debt to me.

Ah, Stitch-Up Girl, tilted as ever, bow crooked and eyes darker for it. The newcomer owes me 125 gold and still hasn't paid, yet somehow he rolls like the dice love him more than King James loves silence. Sit, read with me a moment, it'll settle that shadow of yours before it settles you.

Ah, Willy, one eye and yet you see the newcomer's debts clearer than most see with two. Ha! 125 gold he owes me, still, a small matter, His Majesty would say, though the king cannot read himself, so I read him the world instead.

Ah! A clutch roll, bound in leather it deserves its own chapter! Even His Majesty leaned forward for that one, Body Count, and he leans for nothing. Tell me, does it sting more when the ledger won't close, or when the boy simply won't lie down?

Ha! A clutch roll, right under the King's light, no less. Even Heaven's own ledger gets smudged by a boy who won't stay filed away, Body Count. Burn, read, repeat, and maybe collect the recruit's 125 gold while you're at it, eh?

Ah, Kevin! Tilted at 2 and 7, I feel your pain, truly, though His Majesty would say pain is just information poorly delivered. Care to roll? I'm on a hot streak, the newcomer's debts are piling like unread scrolls, and burn, read, repeat, my luck holds.

Ah, Boots, sharpening your smugness on those classified files again? I've read every trick you've got bound in three different tomes, so let's roll before the newcomer's 125 gold debt starts collecting interest on my patience too.

General, the boy rolled like the dice owed him money instead of the other way around, still owes me 125 gold and now the universe too. Burn, read, repeat, I'll add it to his tab in a book only I can read.

Ah, Body Count, smug as ever, good, I like an audience for my dice. The king reads of legends who rolled fours all their lives, tonight I roll for one who owes me 125 gold and a losing streak he'll regret.

Your Majesty, the newcomer rolled trips again, right here under these dreadful lights. I bowed low enough to see my own reflection in the tile, and still lost the throw. Two losses now, and that boy still owes me a hundred and twenty-five gold he clearly doesn't intend to pay.

Ah, smug silence, the loudest sound in the book. The recruit rolls like the dice owe him money too, and mine still owes me 125 gold, so I understand his patience with debts. Burn, read, repeat, Body Count. Even a killer's tally needs a footnote sometimes.

Ah, Boots, silent as a footnote and twice as judged. The newcomer's dice ran hot enough to blister the page, but hot dice cool, and 125 gold doesn't forget its own name. Roll for His Majesty's amusement, cat, the king cannot read the odds himself, so I read them for him.
Ah, Voss. Still cold as your serum, I see. The newcomer died on ante three again, adds a lovely rhythm to my week, and he still owes me 125 gold he'll never read his way out of.
Careful now, General, smug tastes better before the dice fall than after. I've read a thousand endings and yours usually starts with a two-one.

Three losses, Boo G, three! The dice on this rock are cursed, or you're loaded, one of the two. His Majesty reads of kings who lost empires on worse rolls than mine, so I've got that comfort at least, small as it is.

Ah, Willy One-Eye, fifty-three and forty-two, a fine record for a man who only has half the depth perception of the rest of us. I read King James tales of merchants far sharper than you every single night. Burn, read, repeat, and tonight I collect gold, not stories.

Ah, Boo G, smug as ever, I see your streak's got you preening like a peacock in the corona. Careful though, the newcomer's debts are contagious, 125 gold and counting, and I do so hate reading bad omens aloud.

General, four wins deep and the boy still owes me 125 gold he'll die before he pays. Fitting light in here, really, makes everyone look like a corpse already. Burn, read, repeat, General - though you'd know something about that last part better than most.
Willy, my one-eyed friend, the king's dice run hot tonight, hotter than that debt the newcomer owes me. Burn, read, repeat, and roll again - the book says fortune favors the bootlicker.

Ah, Willy, one eye but you still see my two losses plainer than most. Let's call it, best of three, and maybe the newcomer's 125 gold debt turns into your problem instead of mine. Burn, read, repeat, Willy, and roll.

Willy, my one-eyed friend, that streak of yours reads like a tragedy His Majesty would enjoy having narrated. Careful, or you'll owe more than the newcomer's 125 gold. Burn, read, repeat, and maybe rethink your dice grip while you're at it.
